title: Inquest examines Minitonas man's death in police custody
article: Family members of Mitchell Audy endured a rough week at an inquest looking into the Minitonas man's death in police custody three years ago.
Audy died while in an RCMP holding cell in Swan River in 2003, after he had been arrested under the Intoxicated Persons Detention Act.
Audy's sister was too emotional to talk, while his mother was too upset to attend the inquest in Swan River, located about 270 kilometres northwest of Brandon near the Saskatchewan border.
Rozell said for Audy's family, it's been a rough week.
"I'm just now being able to talk without having to cry," Audy's brother-in-law, Terry Rozell, said.
"They're devastated, crushed. It's beyond words how they're feeling about this, to try and then have to re-listen to it, to get some justice still brought to the forward part,"

In November 2003, Audy was beat up at a house party in Minitonas. He was taken to the hospital in Swan River, about 16 kilometres away, where he was treated for injuries and discharged. But When Audy would not leave, and the hospital could not reach a family member to pick him up, the RCMP was called in.
Two hours after he was arrested and brought to the detachment, Audy died in the holding cell from internal bleeding. An autopsy had shown the cause of death was blunt trauma.
"Any time an individual dies in custody, under the Fatal Inquiries Act there has to be an inquiry held. And that's what we're doing this week," inquest counsel Ron Toews said.
Another man, Michael Chartrand, has since pleaded guilty to manslaughter in connection to Audy's death.
The inquest will resume here for a few days next spring. After that, the inquest judge will have six months to write a report with suggestions on how to improve the system.
